new.md:
Creates a new message dialog.

This is a simple dialog with some text the user may want to see.
When the user clicks a button a “response” signal is emitted with
response IDs from [`ResponseType`](xref:gtk:Gtk.ResponseType). See [`Dialog`](xref:gtk:Gtk.Dialog)
for more details.

new_with_markup.md:
Creates a new message dialog.

This is a simple dialog with some text that is marked up with
Pango markup. When the user clicks a button a “response” signal
is emitted with response IDs from [`ResponseType`](xref:gtk:Gtk.ResponseType). See
[`Dialog`](xref:gtk:Gtk.Dialog) for more details.

Special XML characters in the printf() arguments passed to this
function will automatically be escaped as necessary.
(See g_markup_printf_escaped() for how this is implemented.)
Usually this is what you want, but if you have an existing
Pango markup string that you want to use literally as the
label, then you need to use [`MessageDialog.set_markup()`](xref:gtk:Gtk.MessageDialog#method:set_markup)
instead, since you can’t pass the markup string either
as the format (it might contain “%” characters) or as a string
argument.

```c
GtkWidget *dialog;
GtkDialogFlags flags = GTK_DIALOG_DESTROY_WITH_PARENT;
dialog = gtk_message_dialog_new (parent_window,
                                 flags,
                                 GTK_MESSAGE_ERROR,
                                 GTK_BUTTONS_CLOSE,
                                 NULL);
gtk_message_dialog_set_markup (GTK_MESSAGE_DIALOG (dialog),
                               markup);
```

doc.brief: `GtkMessageDialog` presents a dialog with some message text.
doc.md:
`GtkMessageDialog` presents a dialog with some message text.

It’s simply a convenience widget; you could construct the equivalent of
`GtkMessageDialog` from `GtkDialog` without too much effort, but
`GtkMessageDialog` saves typing.

The easiest way to do a modal message dialog is to use the %GTK_DIALOG_MODAL
flag, which will call [`Window.set_modal()`](xref:gtk:Gtk.Window#method:set_modal) internally. The dialog will
prevent interaction with the parent window until it's hidden or destroyed.
You can use the [`Dialog::response`](xref:gtk:Gtk.Dialog#event:response) signal to know when the user
dismissed the dialog.

An example for using a modal dialog:
```c
GtkDialogFlags flags = GTK_DIALOG_DESTROY_WITH_PARENT | GTK_DIALOG_MODAL;
dialog = gtk_message_dialog_new (parent_window,
                                 flags,
                                 GTK_MESSAGE_ERROR,
                                 GTK_BUTTONS_CLOSE,
                                 "Error reading “%s”: %s",
                                 filename,
                                 g_strerror (errno));
// Destroy the dialog when the user responds to it
// (e.g. clicks a button)

g_signal_connect (dialog, "response",
                  G_CALLBACK (gtk_window_destroy),
                  NULL);
```

You might do a non-modal `GtkMessageDialog` simply by omitting the
%GTK_DIALOG_MODAL flag:

```c
GtkDialogFlags flags = GTK_DIALOG_DESTROY_WITH_PARENT;
dialog = gtk_message_dialog_new (parent_window,
                                 flags,
                                 GTK_MESSAGE_ERROR,
                                 GTK_BUTTONS_CLOSE,
                                 "Error reading “%s”: %s",
                                 filename,
                                 g_strerror (errno));

// Destroy the dialog when the user responds to it
// (e.g. clicks a button)
g_signal_connect (dialog, "response",
                  G_CALLBACK (gtk_window_destroy),
                  NULL);
```

# GtkMessageDialog as GtkBuildable

The `GtkMessageDialog` implementation of the `GtkBuildable` interface exposes
the message area as an internal child with the name “message_area”.

format_secondary_markup.brief: Sets the secondary text of the message dialog.

format_secondary_text.brief: Sets the secondary text of the message dialog.
format_secondary_text.md: Sets the secondary text of the message dialog.

get_message_area.brief: Returns the message area of the dialog.
get_message_area.md:
Returns the message area of the dialog.

This is the box where the dialog’s primary and secondary labels
are packed. You can add your own extra content to that box and it
will appear below those labels. See [`Dialog.get_content_area()`](xref:gtk:Gtk.Dialog#method:get_content_area)
for the corresponding function in the parent [`Dialog`](xref:gtk:Gtk.Dialog).

set_markup.brief: Sets the text of the message dialog.
set_markup.md: Sets the text of the message dialog.

buttons.brief: Set of buttons to display on the dialog.
buttons.md: Set of buttons to display on the dialog.

message-area.brief: The `GtkBox` that corresponds to the message area of this dialog.
message-area.md:
The `GtkBox` that corresponds to the message area of this dialog.

See [`MessageDialog.get_message_area()`](xref:gtk:Gtk.MessageDialog#method:get_message_area) for a detailed
description of this area.

secondary-text.brief: The secondary text of the message dialog.
secondary-text.md: The secondary text of the message dialog.

secondary-use-markup.brief: `TRUE` if the secondary text of the dialog includes Pango markup.
secondary-use-markup.md:

See `parse_markup`.

text.brief: The primary text of the message dialog.
text.md:
The primary text of the message dialog.

If the dialog has a secondary text, this will appear as the title.
